identificationModule.briefTitle: Phase II Study of Tislelizumab Combined With Cetuximab and Irinotecan in the Treatment of Recurrent, Refractory mCRC
identificationModule.officialTitle: Phase II Clinical Study on the Efficacy and Safety of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Combined With Cetuximab and Irinotecan in the Treatment of Recurrent, Refractory and Metastatic Colorectal Cancer

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This is a single arm, open phase II study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of tislelizumab combined with cetuximab + irinotecan in the treatment of Ras wild-type recurrent and refractory colorectal cancer. This study will include Ras wild-type colorectal cancer that failed at least second-line treatment in the past, including chemotherapy (oxaliplatin, irinotecan, fluorouracil) with or without targeted drugs (cetuximab, bevacizumab). 33 patients were planned to be treated with tislelizumab combined with cetuximab + irinotecan every 2 weeks. The enrollment time is expected to be 12 months and the follow-up is 24 months.
